recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not restore the original broad "primarily used" FHIR-26368 wording because later FHIR-26390 work intentionally replaced it with clearer limited-use guidance. Consider FHIR-57354 separately when Resolved - change required issues are in scope.
issue_request: FHIR-26368 was Published with resolution Persuasive. It asked FHIR-I to remove the Parameters language saying the resource had no other use outside operations, because that appeared to prevent Parameters from being used in a messaging Bundle, especially as MessageHeader.focus.
initial_application: The original source change was made by 6275ee6723bf77b15313933ea4c7b5fa927d12cd and merged by a410a74438d69a8f66d0dee3dd433dad31169128, changing the Parameters resource description to remove "It has no other use." The broader Parameters/messaging family was later refined through FHIR-26390 implementation commits and PR #1957.
additional_context: FHIR-26390 is a Published follow-up that narrowed the broad FHIR-26368 relaxation into explicit limited-use allowances, including MessageHeader.focus, and the combined branch already contains the FHIR-26390 reconciliation commit 4f2edddd4a388a76f071bb8b4f1f6f3ba7d1a743. FHIR-57354 is a later Resolved - change required request to remove the Bundle.entry.resource guardrail, but that status is outside this default Applied/Published edit scope.
reconciliation: No source file was changed. Current build-scope source already says Parameters can pass information into and back from operations invoked directly from REST or within messaging, explicitly allows MessageHeader.focus to be a Parameters resource, and lacks the old "It has no other use" wording in the relevant source directories.

related_jiras.note: Published follow-up that constrained the FHIR-26368 Parameters relaxation to explicit limited-use allowances and is already represented on the combined branch.
2026 Resolved - change required issue targeting only the Bundle.entry.resource Parameters guardrail; related context but not decided in this default Applied/Published run.
